key_insight: The paper argues that weak geometric representations in encoder-based novel view synthesis are not mainly caused by insufficient supervision. Instead, the real issue is that overly expressive spatial decoders absorb too much of the reconstruction burden, preventing the encoder from learning strong 3D scene representations.
problem_solved: It addresses the gap between novel view synthesis performance and the quality of learned geometric representations, especially why encoder-based NVS methods often fail to produce transferable multi-view features.
method: Analyze encoder-based novel view synthesis through the lens of geometric representation learning.
Show that spatially expressive decoders can weaken the encoder’s incentive to encode scene structure.
Motivate architectural designs that shift more responsibility for 3D understanding back to the encoder.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this reframes NVS design: better geometric features may come less from adding supervision and more from choosing the right encoder-decoder balance. This can improve downstream transfer to tasks that need robust 3D scene understanding.
visual_elements: Encoder-decoder architecture diagram highlighting where 3D information is learned

Flow chart showing how expressive decoders dilute encoder learning

paper_title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Keerthi Kaashyap, Dennis Anthony, Akshay Krishnan, Nhi Ngoc Nguyen, Jeremy Collins
